If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in late horizon (day 25–30) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in mid horizon (day 15–24) to compensate for bearish bias.  
If sentiment swings sharply (≥0.67 then ≤0.33 or vice versa) within last 5 days, apply a 2% downward correction to forecast at day 10–14 to dampen volatility-induced overfitting.  
If forecast exceeds true value by >3% in early horizon (day 1–5) and sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), apply a 1.5% downward adjustment starting day 6 to align with mean reversion.  
If true price rises >2% from day 10–14 and sentiment remains positive, apply a 1% upward bias to forecast from day 15 onward to capture momentum.  
If forecast consistently underestimates true price in late horizon (day 25–30) despite neutral sentiment, apply a 1.5% upward adjustment to offset lagged model drift.
